stem:
Meera brings the North pole of a bar magnet close to the North pole of another bar magnet lying on her study table at home.
What will happen to the two poles?

options.text: They will attract each other because magnets always attract.
They will repel each other because like poles repel.
They will attract each other because one magnet is stronger.
Nothing will happen because the magnets are not touching.

teacher.key_rationale: Like poles (N–N) repel each other, so B is correct. A is the trap for the idea that magnets always attract; C incorrectly links attraction to strength; D wrongly requires contact for magnetic force.
